note: Spec 23 Food Compass live lens, P0-P6. Rebuilds Scott Black's One Good Choice capability on this codebase's rule that the model never computes numbers: 9,273 published Food Compass 2.0 scores extracted from Table S5 plus 6,150 joined FNDDS 2017-18 nutrient panels, a deterministic TypeScript scoring engine, a live camera loop, the score on /food and in the meal log, and a standalone shareable /compass preview with a realtime voice tool that looks scores up rather than recalling them. The three discrepancy-ledger items were resolved empirically before any engine code was written, against a clean subset of 110 foods whose D4/D5 contributions are provably zero: dairy half-weight is halve-then-plain-average (dairy r 0.919 vs 0.847), D7 top-3 is a weighted mean (bcMAE 2.70 vs 3.35), and the nitrite 25-vs-50% question is not discriminable with the available data and is recorded as such rather than guessed. Also fixes three defects found on the way: the storage guard would have silently dropped every pre-spec-23 meal-log entry, the live loop could enter an unbounded request loop against a paid endpoint, and 'partially hydrogenated soybean oil' counted as two binary additives instead of one. note: Spec 26 P6, the namespace move. The public door is now /food/demo, under the product it is a door onto; /compass is a permanent 308 in next.config.mjs beside the existing /family -> /ladder one, and Next carries the query string so links already shared keep working. src/app/compass/{page,layout,title,page.test} moved to src/app/food/demo/ with page.tsx and layout.tsx byte-identical; e2e/compass.spec.ts became e2e/food-demo.spec.ts; check-compass-store-free.mjs became check-public-door-store-free.mjs. THE MOVE CREATED ONE RISK AND CLOSED IT: at /compass the door inherited only the app root layout, but at /food/demo it also inherits anything at src/app/food/layout.tsx -- a file that does not exist today, would apply to the public door without appearing in its own directory, and is exactly where someone would reach for a provider. The witness now walks the inherited wrapper chain (layout.tsx AND template.tsx, since a template wraps children the same way) with the app root the one documented exception. That walk finds nothing today, which made it the easiest thing in the file to delete silently, so --self-test drives it off a stub tree and one function builds the whole seed; five mutations were run against it and all five are caught. THREE THINGS A REVIEW OF THE MOVE FOUND, all fixed here: (1) Next merges metadata field by field, so the demo layout declaring only a title kept the root layout's manifest and icons -- installing the shared link offered 'My Health' with the patient icon and opened /today. /ladder hit this first and fixed it the same way; the public door now ships food-lens.webmanifest (start_url /food/demo, scope / so the /compass redirect resolves inside the installed window) and food-lens-icon.svg, pinned by src/app/food/demo/layout.test.tsx. (2) The public-door runbook still scripted a text box and a 'Play voice example' button, neither of which has existed since spec 25 turned typedInput off -- six of eight steps were unexecutable; rewritten to camera-on-load and spoken input. (3) Three capability flags were declared and read nowhere: sampleScan duplicated the hard-coded demoPreview prop, and plate and personalized read as enforcement while enforcing nothing -- all three deleted, with the type header now recording that the real enforcement is the import-graph proof rather than a boolean a future edit can forget. Also retired 15 comments and two test URLs that still named /compass as a live route, including one in food-compass-data.ts that named a budget key P6 had changed. KNOWN, PRE-EXISTING, STILL OPEN, now reproduced on the new path: the root layout mounts HealthStateProvider around every route, so a visitor to the public link gets home-health-ai-ownership-state written to their localStorage. Confirmed live on /food/demo, and it is also the cause of a React #418 hydration error that appears only after that key exists -- a fresh context with empty storage has a clean console. The page imports none of that state and renders none of it, so decision 5 holds as written, but it still wants an owner call.

note: Spec 27 Plate scan, P0-P5, plus spec 28 package label scan which landed on master from a concurrent session and had no ledger line of its own. PLATE SCAN: POST /api/food/plate decomposes one photo into at most five discrete foods. The model names foods and estimates mass in grams and nothing else -- every number a patient sees is still the published ledger row the name resolved to. Model spend is pinned by route tests: one call when every name is confident, exactly two when any is not (all unconfident names ride ONE batched disambiguation call), never one per item. Carve-outs are per item, so a glass of water cannot swallow the plate. Portions snap to half-steps of the 100 g ledger basis; Half that / About right / Double it correct them in one tap, and the first correction of any kind flips the portion to the patient's own, which retires the chips and the carb range. The chips deliberately do not snap: halving 1.5 to 0.75 and doubling back has to land on 1.5 exactly. HONEST CARBS: a photo-derived carb number renders as a band (+/-30%, rounded outward to 5 g) computed at render time from the unscaled row; logged entries keep the point estimate, so summarizeDayTotals and computeFoodFlags are untouched and nothing new is persisted anywhere. The hedge under it ('Never use them for insulin math; follow your care team's plan') is backed by code, not vibes: verifyGrounding now blocks dose-calculation help and allergy/child clearance, anchored on dose math inside ONE sentence (an insulin term + a computation verb + a digit) rather than proximity to a bare 'for'. That anchoring is load-bearing -- a looser pattern would match the hedge this app prints itself and the existing 'do not stop or change the dose' note, silently swapping every compliant answer for the generic fallback. Both are pinned as must-pass corpus cases in safety-gate.test.ts, which is inside crisis:gate. The same two rules land in all three places a food answer can come from: GROUNDING_SAFE_PHRASING (typed vision, pantry, compass), the base section list in buildFoodLensInstructions (what the realtime voice session actually uses), and output-guard.ts, which never runs verifyGrounding. ONE-QUESTION REFINE: plate-refine.ts detects candidates that differ from the matched row ONLY by a fat-preparation qualifier, reading FNDDS as it is actually written -- 'cooked with oil' and 'cooked, no added fat' reduce to the same core, and the real 'no addded fat' typo in the table is absorbed rather than dropped. At most one question per scan, on the item where the answer moves the most calories, answered by the same zero-spend re-score-by-food-code the correction chips use. DEVIATION FROM THE SPEC AS WRITTEN, deliberate: P1 said matched items append straight to the plate. They no longer do. A concurrent session's spec 28 established a confirmation-first invariant app-wide (no score before the patient confirms a named row), and 9f22ad9 brought the plate scan under it: a scan now produces a review list and nothing is scored or added until a row is tapped. That is a stricter reading of the same safety goal, so it stands. ONE REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED AT SHIP TIME (6181f82): 9f22ad9 stripped the abort registration and authority-epoch check from correctPlateItem while leaving them on its sibling addPlateItemByFoodId. Two quick chip taps on one plate item raced and the slower response won, so the item could end up showing a food the patient had not chosen. Restored to mirror the sibling exactly, sharing one plate-choice abort ref. KNOWN, PRE-EXISTING, STILL OPEN: the root layout mounts HealthStateProvider around every route, so a visitor to the public /food/demo link still gets the fictional demo patient written to their localStorage. Unchanged by this work and still wants an owner call.
